POST prism/comment-lookup.desc: Re-check up to 25 known comments in one call: per-item results, failed items refunded.
POST prism/comment-lookup.label: 2-100 (metered): 2 credits per found TikTok item and 5 per found Instagram item, raised by `deep_scan`. Up to 25 items per call: the whole batch holds at most 100 credits up front and refunds every not_found, errored and deferred item

POST prism/jobs.desc: Up to 5,000 profiles or post URLs in one background job, at the batch endpoints' own prices.
POST prism/jobs.label: The same price per row as the batch endpoint the job runs: prism/profiles (1 credit per profile on most platforms, 5 on LinkedIn, plus 1 per posts page with include: "posts") or prism/post-stats (its per-URL price). The call holds the whole job's worst case up front, answered in credits_used on the 202, and refunds every row that is not ok when the job completes. Reading the job is free.

POST prism/post-stats.desc: Up to 100 mixed-platform post URLs → current engagement per URL, failed URLs refunded.
POST prism/post-stats.label: 1-500 (metered): 1 credit per successful URL on most platforms, 2 on Instagram and 5 on LinkedIn, charged at each URL's own platform rate. Up to 100 URLs per call: the call holds the summed worst case up front (a 100-URL Instagram batch holds 200) and refunds every dead, errored and unsupported URL, so you pay for exactly the rows that returned counts

POST prism/profiles.desc: Up to 50 (platform, handle) pairs → one canonical Author per row, failed handles refunded.
POST prism/profiles.label: 1-250 (metered): 1 credit per successful row on most platforms and 5 on LinkedIn, charged at each handle's own platform tier. Up to 50 items per call: the call holds the summed worst case up front and refunds every not_found, unsupported, errored and deferred row. With include: "posts" (up to 25 items) a row also costs its post list page, 1 credit, charged only when that page came back with posts

POST web/monitors.label: 0 credits to create. Each scheduled check then bills its upstream cost plus 1 credit for orchestration, repeating on `cadence_minutes` until you pause or delete the monitor (a 5-minute cadence is 288 checks a day)

POST web/sessions.label: 20 credits per browser-hour, minimum 5. The hold is taken from `ttl_seconds` when the session is created (60s default = 5, the 3,600s maximum = 20) and settled when it closes

POST youtube/channels.desc: Batch get YouTube channel details (up to 1000)
POST youtube/channels.label: 5-100 (metered): 5 credits per 50-id chunk, so a 50-id batch is 5 credits and the 1,000-id maximum is 100. Batching is what makes this cheap: the same 1,000 channels fetched one at a time through GET /v1/youtube/channel cost 1,000 credits. A chunk is charged whether or not every id in it resolves, so there is no per-id refund; a call that resolves nothing at all is refunded in full

POST youtube/transcripts.desc: Up to 100 YouTube video ids → one transcript per row, failed ids refunded.
POST youtube/transcripts.label: 3-300 (metered): 3 credits per successful transcript. Up to 100 ids per call: the call holds ids × 3 up front (a full batch holds 300) and refunds every not_found, errored and deferred row
